daily-living.notes: Check bath water temperature first, side-lying with little liquid for unconscious mouth care, dentures over a towel- or water-lined sink with cool/lukewarm water and stored wet in a labeled cup, electric razor with blood thinners, weak side dressed first / undressed last (strong side off first), upright small-bite feeding, NPO = nothing by mouth, thickened liquids for dysphagia, front-to-back perineal care, drainage bag below the bladder and off the floor, catheter tubing cleaned from the body outward, report black tarry stool, no aide toenail cutting with diabetes, pressure injuries over bony areas and never rub reddened areas: all match standard nurse aide practice. Plain English, no regulatory figures (no source needed).

infection-control.notes: Matches CDC: hand hygiene is the most important measure, alcohol-based rub for most routine care, soap and water when hands are visibly soiled, gloves do not replace hand hygiene, clean hands after removing gloves, change gloves between residents and from dirty to clean task. Standard precautions for all; contact = gown + gloves, droplet = mask (influenza), airborne = AIIR with door closed + fitted N95 (TB). PPE donning order gown -> mask/respirator -> goggles/face shield -> gloves matches the CDC sequence. Hand-hygiene card carries a CDC source. Advisory only (not a FAIL): CDC 2007 Isolation Guideline says to put on the mask on entry to the room; 'staff wear a mask when close to the resident' could become 'staff wear a mask when entering the room'.

safety-emergency.notes: Bed low, wheels locked, call light in reach, non-skid footwear, ID band check, ease a falling resident to the floor protecting the head, do not move a resident found on the floor and call the nurse, abdominal thrusts only when the person cannot speak/cough/breathe and encourage a strong cough, seizure care (protect head, loosen clothing, do not restrain, nothing in the mouth), RACE and PASS, oxygen supports combustion and the aide does not change the flow rate, unplug by the plug: all correct.

positioning-mobility.notes: Body mechanics (feet about shoulder-width, bend knees and hips, back straight, load close, pivot the feet instead of twisting, push/pull rather than lift, bed at working height), supine/prone/Fowler's/Sims' (left side, semi-prone, upper leg bent toward chest), logrolling, lift sheet with two workers, brakes locked, wheelchair on the strong side, gait belt at the waist over clothing snug with finger room, walk on the weak side slightly behind: all correct. Figure body-mechanics-compare.svg checked below (PASS).

restorative-care.notes: Promote independence, ROM slow and gentle with the joint supported and stop for pain, passive vs active ROM, cane on the strong side moved with the weak leg (weak left leg -> cane in right hand), standard walker moved forward a short distance then step, bladder training on a regular schedule without scolding, built-up utensils/plate guards/reachers, check residual-limb skin when a prosthesis is removed: all correct.

vital-signs.notes: Adult resting pulse 60-100/min, respirations 12-20/min, radial pulse on the thumb side of the wrist, irregular pulse counted for a full 60 seconds, count respirations without the resident noticing, average oral temperature about 98.6 F (37 C), rectal highest / axillary lowest, normal BP below 120 and below 80 mm Hg (AHA 'Normal' category, card carries an AHA source), small cuff gives a falsely high reading, I&O counts items liquid at room temperature, 1 oz = 30 mL (standard rounding), weigh at the same time/scale/clothing, pain is what the resident reports: all correct. The compare table matches the cards.

emotional-mental-health.notes: Maslow order (physiological, safety, love/belonging, esteem, self-actualization), Alzheimer's is the most common cause of dementia and is progressive, short simple sentences, approach from the front, redirect and validate feelings rather than argue, sundowning in the late afternoon/evening, Kubler-Ross five stages in any order, hearing thought to be among the last senses lost, report signs of depression and stay with a resident who talks of self-harm, locking a resident in a room = involuntary seclusion: all correct.

spiritual-cultural.notes: Privacy for prayer and clergy, ask before moving religious items, ask how the resident wants to be addressed, respect religious/cultural food rules and report so a substitute is given, never impose or mock beliefs: all correct standard practice.

communication.notes: Verbal vs nonverbal, active listening, open-ended questions, hearing loss (face the resident, speak clearly at a normal or slightly lower pitch, do not shout), vision loss (say your name on entering and tell the resident when you leave), aphasia after stroke (yes/no questions, extra time, pictures/gestures), objective reporting with the resident's words in quotes, paper error correction with a single line + initials + date and no erasing/white-out, 24-hour time (3:00 p.m. = 1500), barriers (medical terms, noise, giving advice): all correct.

client-rights.notes: eCFR checked (42 CFR Part 483, up to date as of 2026-10-28): 483.10(c)(6) right to request, refuse, and/or discontinue treatment; 483.10(h) heading is 'Privacy and confidentiality' (source paragraph correct); 483.12(a)(2) free from physical or chemical restraints imposed for discipline or convenience and not required to treat medical symptoms, and when used, the least restrictive alternative for the least amount of time; 483.12(c)(1) report not later than 2 hours if the allegation involves abuse or results in serious bodily injury, otherwise not later than 24 hours; 483.12(c)(4) results within 5 working days. Choices, belongings, unopened mail, grievances without reprisal, involuntary seclusion as abuse also correct. Every card with a regulatory figure carries a source.

legal-ethical.notes: eCFR checked: 483.152(a)(1) no less than 75 clock hours and (a)(3) at least 16 hours of supervised practical training; 483.156(c)(1) registry lists individuals who completed a NATCEP (483.152) or CEP (483.154) and includes findings of abuse, neglect, or misappropriation of property; 483.35(d)(6) 'Required retraining': 24 consecutive months with no nursing or nursing-related services for monetary compensation -> new training and competency evaluation program or new competency evaluation program (paragraph letter correct in the current text). Scope of practice, negligence vs neglect, mental abuse by threats to withhold food/care, misappropriation including 'borrowing', refusing tips, no social-media posting: all correct. Sources present on all regulatory cards.

care-team.notes: eCFR checked: 483.95(g)(1) in-service no less than 12 hours per year and (g)(2) must include dementia management and resident abuse prevention training; card source 42 CFR 483.95(g) correct (483.35(d)(7) also points to 483.95(g)). Licensed nurse (RN or LPN/LVN) supervises the aide, care plan, chain of command, PT = strength and walking, SLP = speech, language, and swallowing, refuse untrained tasks and tell the nurse: all correct.

body-mechanics-compare.svg.checklist: ① PASS ② PASS ③ PASS ④ N/A (concept figure) ⑤ PASS
body-mechanics-compare.svg.notes: ① Viewed reports/images-png/cna-nurse-aide/body-mechanics-compare.png: two black stick figures on white with a divider, bold headings 'Poor body mechanics' / 'Good body mechanics', and two-line labels under each; no clipped or overlapping text, readable at phone width. ② Plain stick figures, box, and floor line; no invented symbols. ③ Left: legs straight, trunk bent forward to horizontal, reaching to a box on the floor in front = poor; right: feet apart, knees bent, trunk upright, box held against the chest = good; both are correct body mechanics teaching. ⑤ Matches the chapter's concepts (wide base, knees bent, back straight, load close) and the summary; caption 'Poor and good body mechanics when lifting a load' and alt text match what is drawn; source kind self. Minor drawing note (not a FAIL): the good figure looks partly like a half-squat/lunge after the lift rather than mid-lift; it does not contradict the text.
